content.title: When Does The Pitt Season 2 Episode 10 Drop on HBO Max?
content.text: Andy Silva breaks down everything you need to know for the 10th episode of the second season of the critically acclaimed HBO Max show, starring Noah Wyle. The Pitt Season 2 Episode 10 premieres on Thursday, March 12, 2026, at 9 p.m. ET on HBO Max. Things got a bit dark last week, with several stories taking a turn for the worse. Between the kid who blew off two fingers with a firecracker, Howard facing a 50-50 chance of survival and terminally ill Roxie confronting her mortality, there wasn’t a ton of light to be found in Episode 9. And that was before the last second revelation of an accident at a water park sure to flood PTMC with even more patients. Things look like they’re only going to get worse before they get better for Dr. Robby and his crew. The Pitt Season 2 Episode 10 Preview For the first time in a while, I think I agree with Ogilvie — PTMC’s Pitt and The Pitt are relentless. In addition to their ongoing IT shutdown, now trauma patients will be coming in as a result of an accident at a water park. This looks like it will put Santos into the uncomfortable position of working with Langdon, although Garcia notes that Santos is going to have to get used to it because Langdon is here to stay. Meanwhile, Victoria has to deal with more fallout from her near fatal mistake in Episode 9 in the form of her mother, who notes that Victoria’s better than this. And while Robby is right that the ED is not for the faint of heart, it’s hard to argue with Dr. Al-Hashimi that he needs to refind his sense of empathy a bit. Laughing at the comment is probably not the best place to start. And Dr. Mohan looks like she’s about to go from doctor to patient amid all the chaos. Like Mohan, we’re going to have to go along for the ride as business looks like it’s about to pick up even more at PTMC. The Pitt Season 2 Episode 9 Recap (Warning: Spoilers ahead.) Chaos is still the word of the day as the episode begins. Dropped in amongst this all is 12-year-old Jude, who has suffered a serious hand injury in a fireworks accident. So serious in fact that he blew two of his fingers to bits. Luckily for him he dropped it fast enough to save the rest of the hand, but needless to say Jude is freaking out. Of course, there is more to the story as Santos smells alcohol on his breath. It turns out that his blood alcohol level is a .08 (there are some older boys who are bad influences in the building), which mandates a social services consult. Making the situation even more challenging is that Jude is being cared for by his older sister, Chantal, as their parents were deported to Haiti as part of the ongoing immigration crackdown. Jude’s sister is trying to balance her school work, work and taking care of Jude, but as she notes it’s a lot easier being a big sister than a surrogate mom. Moreover, she promised their parents that she wouldn’t let them separate her and Jude, so she gets defensive when Robby and Santos mention social services. The interview goes well, but even with that being the case there is no guarantee that Jude won’t be put into foster care. As I noted earlier in the seasonopens in a new tab, The Pitt‘s spiritual predecessor ER regularly addressed social issues, so it’s not surprising for the current situation regarding immigration to become part of a storyline. Really, given everything happening in the real world, it would be hard to ignore it. It’s the second instance this season of real-world fallout from the 2024 presidential election impacting a storyline and I would bet it may not be the last. One of the lone bright spots this week is that we appear to get some good news for the patient who suffered an eye stroke. It appears Dr. Al’s risky treatment plan is paying off, as she sees subtle signs of sight improvement. Her vision has improved to 20/200, but it’s much better than it had been and Mel notes that it could improve over time. It’s not all good news for Mel, however, as her sister Becca is waiting for her in chairs with a bellyache. Mel is still freaking out about her upcoming deposition, so this only further freaks her out more. Just as she is getting her sister set up the hospital’s lawyer arrives to bring her to the deposition. Langdon takes over Becca’s care and does well with her, remembering the lessons he learned from Mel last season when dealing with neurodivergent patients. Becca also makes clear that Mel talks about work at home, showing excitement to meet Robby and noting that Mel says lots of nice things about Langdon. Amaya, a patient with PCOS, is being seen by McKay for abdominal pain. The patient notes that she had years of pain and hormonal changes before being diagnosed with PCOS because it took a long time to find a doctor who actually listened to her. McKay tries to note that sometimes it can take time to find the right diagnosis, but the patient dismisses that as lazy doctoring especially considering that some doctors don’t listen to women, especially woman of color. Her tests look good and Whitaker is ready to send her home with pain meds to free up the bed, but McKay wants to continue to monitor her given that she had more pain than in previous episodes and didn’t look good in triage. Thankfully McKay did, as the patient takes a turn for the worst, with her pain reaching a 12 due to a twisted ovary. Now she will need surgery, but luckily McKay wanted to not repeat the mistakes of the patient’s previous doctors and made the call to continue to monitor the patient, which Whitaker points out to the patient. McKay’s terminal cancer patient Roxie is also having a rough go of it. She can’t hide her pain anymore, not even when presented the opportunity to have an ice cream party with her kids. Roxie admits that she’s struggling with the idea she won’t see her sons grow up, feeling that her life has become a cruel joke. She has a family she loves only to have it ripped away from her by lung cancer, when she didn’t ever even smoke. Roxie asks McKay if she believes in God (she likes the concept) and given her exposure to a fair share of death asks if McKay has any advice as she’s never died before. We don’t hear McKay’s response, but the scene reminded me of an episode of Scrubs I recently wrote aboutopens in a new tab from the show’s eighth season, where J.D. and Turk help a terminal patient of their own come to terms with the fact he’s nearing death. I think their advice remains applicable here — I agree that I’d want my last thought to be a good one. Santos is again hit with slight rejection from Garcia, noting that she made other plans for the Fourth. She reminds Santos that they’re just keeping things casual. It feels like something is here since we’ve seen Garcia brush off Santos a couple of times now. Then Mel’s patients get dumped on her while she is off for her deposition, meaning Santos’ charting will get pushed to post shift. However, Santos does have something of a meet cute with a heat-exhausted Furry from Anthrocon, Pittsburgh’s annual Furry convention. If things don’t work out with Garcia, perhaps Santos can find love outside the hospital. And for the record, I agree that Santos would make a good dragon. The ongoing IT outage requires some old school thinking. Unfortunately, most of the Pitt crew have no clue what a fax machine or toner is (ah, to be young) and feel like they’re in hell. Luckily, Dana makes some calls and pulls in “retired” old school clerk Monica, who immediately begins cracking the whip and picking right back up where she left off before she became a casualty of the digital revolution. In a season where Dr. Al is pushing her AI charting tool, it feels like the presence of this old-school clerk is a reminder that there is a human cost to relying so heavily on technological advances and it’s always good to have a fallback to rely on when you have to go analog. Speaking of the ongoing IT outage, Victoria is having a hard time adjusting to life without the electronic boards. She drops the ball on marking her patient, Mrs. Burns, on the board and it nearly turns into a fatal mistake as the patient crashes. She’s unresponsive when Victoria goes to present her case to Whitaker and seeing what happened clearly rattles Victoria. Since the patient wasn’t on the board her orders never went to lab (Dana points out if the patient isn’t on the board they don’t exist), but her X-ray was available on the portable machine. And good thing because it shows that she needs surgery stat. Garcia is pissed (even going so far as to call Victoria a nepo baby) and the news only gets worse as Victoria’s mother will be operating. It’s a tough hour for Victoria. Mohan and Ogilvie see a patient dealing with flank pain, which hits a bit close to home for Ogilvie as the patient is an English teacher like his father. Interestingly, there seems to be some estrangement between Ogilvie and his dad, as when the patient notes that his dad must be proud all Ogilvie can muster is you’d have to ask him. Perhaps Ogilvie’s off-putting behavior all season has been a case of overcompensating for a lack of love at home. It certainly opens up the possibility that there is more to Ogilvie than meets the eye. In an attempt to be helpful, Dr. Al brought radiology to the ED, but between how much space Dr. Barker is taking up and how much he is distracting some of the female staff (especially Princess), he is turning into more of a hindrance than a help. Emma and Dana have a nice moment where Dana tells Emma she did good with their sexual assault patient. Emma’s smart response to think about the potential of a time where she wishes she could change her mind and press charges got the patient back into the room. Dana looks like a proud parent while noting that Emma is almost finished with what will be the first of many shifts as a nurse. It’s interesting that the exchange takes place in the same spot where Dana got attacked last season. Perhaps, this is a sign that she can let the incident go and move on. Only time will tell though. Speaking of returns, Howard returns from Presby and he officially needs surgery. Garcia notes that there is a 100 percent chance of death without surgery … and still a 50 percent chance with it. Despite the risks, he wants to speak to his sister before having the surgery. It’s heartbreaking to see Howard and his sister try to mend whatever issues they had in the past quickly in case this is their final conversation. You can see that it affects Howard’s care team as well. We can only hope that he’ll get a chance to make good on those plans to get together with his sister and nephew for the holidays. Abbot returned with Howard and has a chance to catch up with Robby before he heads out on sabbatical. After noting that he likes Dr. Al and that Robby is leaving the day shift in good hands, Abbot notes that he’s still surprised Robby is going on this sabbatical as he can’t remember him even taking three straight days off. Abbot wants to make sure Robby can handle all that time of self-reflection and that if he can’t to remember to call him. Amid all this, Whitaker finally gets his official “doctor” badge from Robby, who uses the moment they have in the break room to inquire about Whitaker’s relationship with the burn victim widow Amy. Robby notes that while it’s good to have empathy, Whitaker also needs to set boundaries. He doesn’t want to see Whitaker taken advantage of. Which leads him to suggest that Whitaker house sit for him while he’s on sabbatical, which Whitaker jumps at. Just no babies allowed at Robby’s bachelor pad. We can only hope that Robby was joking that it could be Whitaker’s if he doesn’t return, but it’s interesting to see him joke about that after he never really acknowledges Abbot when he tells Robby to just make sure he comes back. So, a bit of a downer episode from Shawn Hatosy, who of course also plays Abbot. There were some moments of light, but overall things look a bit bleak at the moment, especially with another major trauma event looking like it’s about to hit the Pitt. That’s not to say it was a bad episode, but it definitely moved some pieces on the chess board as we approach the home stretch of the season. The Pitt FAQ What time do new episodes of The Pitt drop? New episodes of The Pitt drop on Thursdays at 9 p.m. ET. How can I watch new episodes of The Pitt ? The Pitt — including all of season 1 and season 2 to this point — is available to stream on HBO Max. Clips and behind-the-scenes featurettes are also uploaded to the HBO Max YouTube pageopens in a new tab. How many new episodes of The Pitt will drop in season 2? Season 2 of The Pitt is expected to include 15 episodes, with the season set to conclude on April 16, 2026.
